record_kind: public projection of a predeclared controlled whole-product comparison

design.analysis: tools perf_analyze.py: per workload, candidate/baseline ns/op ratio per seed; geometric mean; 95% t interval on log ratios (df 9; normality assumed, not established); exact two-sided sign test; no multiplicity adjustment; all samples retained. Allocation and B/op comparisons per pair. CPU load is recorded before and after each task; no task is rerun or dropped.
design.run_cwd: baseline checkout internal/gtsadapter for both endpoints (benchmark input blobs identical in both trees)
design.host_condition: Run after the local gate and packaging runs finish and while both worker panes are idle; other processes on the host are not controlled.
design.claim_limit: Observation for these two identities only. No speed claim is made unless the interval excludes 1 for a workload, and even then it is exploratory.

interpretation: Exploratory per-workload paired log 95% t interval (df=9) assumes normally distributed log ratios, which ten pairs cannot establish; no multiplicity adjustment; all samples retained. The source, runtime and grammar bundle change together, so this is not an isolated algorithm comparison.
limits: CPU load on the host varied during the run (see cpu_load_percent); latency intervals are exploratory.
B/op and allocation counters are Go heap measurements, not OS RSS.
No claim applies to another runtime, grammar or benchmark identity.
omitted_fields: the plan purpose text (summarized in baseline and candidate)
cpu_load_note: One sample before and one after each of the 20 runs; not continuous load.
ratio_definition: candidate ns/op divided by baseline ns/op per seed; above 1 means main 2d1e93d was slower.
